title: Eugene Bullard: Foreign Legion colonel and fighter
summary: Butler describes Gene Bullard, a Georgian who fled after killing men, joined the Foreign Legion, became a World War I ace, and defended Black people from Red Grange.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: He was the most fascinating individual I have ever met and another one, Frisco --John Bingham. I'll never forget these people gave me wisdom and then this Gene, he came and he was from Georgia somewhere he became a colonel in the Foreign Legion and it seems as though years ago, Gene and some of those caucasians down there had a little trouble and seems like someone said, get him, and it seemed like he left like 12 or 13 dead in the cornfields and made it, made it to France and joined the Foreign Legion and when you join the Foreign Legion, everything is erased.
He seemed to have been so bad and rough that he became colonel in the Foreign Legion.

And then, in World War I, it seemed like he became an ace -- his name is Gene, Eugene Jacques Bullard. And he became an ace, he was bugging the Germans and they was looking for him in the Second World War and so Gene was a very good friend -- well, he used to like me.

And everyone who had trouble -- like, it seems that Red Grange, the football player, was over there bothering people of color and they'd go and get Gene and Gene would go over and speak to Mr. Grange -- Gene, he didn't weight but about 160 lbs. but he did all types of fighting.
So, seemed like they rumbled for hours but Gene picked up a table and tore the man's skull up so that was all. Red Grange -- but, now here's two things that I saw happen to Gene.
